title: Application for a stay of execution of sentence of death

pages.text:
No. ________________
IN THE
SUPREME COURT OF THE UNITED STATES
____________________________
JAMAAL HOWARD,
Petitioner,
v.
TEXAS,
Respondent.
____________________________
On Petition for a Writ of Certiorari
to the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals
____________________________
MOTION FOR STAY OF EXECUTION
____________________________
Petitioner Jamaal Howard is scheduled to be executed tomorrow, October 7, 2026, after 
6:00 p.m. central time. He has filed in this Court a Petition for a Writ of Certiorari seeking review 
of the October 5, 2026, order of the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals (“CCA”) dismissing his 
claim that he is intellectually disabled and therefore ineligible for execution under Atkins v. 
Virginia, 536 U.S. 304 (2002). Howard asks this Court to stay his execution pending its 
consideration and disposition of that petition.
A stay is warranted if there is (1) a reasonable probability that four Justices will consider 
the issue sufficiently meritorious to grant certiorari, (2) a fair prospect that a majority of the 
Court will vote to reverse the judgment below, and (3) a likelihood that irreparable harm will

result from the denial of a stay. Hollingsworth v. Perry, 558 U.S. 183, 190 (2010) (per curiam). 
Each is present here. The petition presents a question about the effect of changing clinical 
standards on Atkins claims, and this Court has already granted certiorari in a case concerning that 
effect. Guerrero v. Johnson, No. 25-1003 (U.S. cert. granted June 15, 2026). No court has ever 
decided whether Howard is intellectually disabled under the clinical standards that govern today. 
Under those standards, his full-scale IQ of 74 and the sworn testimony from his 2001 trial
describing his adaptive deficits at ages 20 and 21 make far more than the threshold showing 
required to have his claim heard. The CCA could conclude otherwise only by measuring 
Howard’s evidence against a diagnostic framework the medical community has discarded, and 
this Court’s decisions forbid that. Hall v. Florida, 572 U.S. 701, 721 (2014); Moore v. Texas, 581 
U.S. 1, 20 (2017). If a stay is not granted, Howard will suffer irreparable harm, because he will be 
executed before this Court can decide whether the Eighth Amendment forbids his execution.
Howard therefore asks the Court to stay his execution, currently scheduled for October 7, 
2026, pending its consideration and disposition of his Petition for a Writ of Certiorari.

DATE: October 6, 2026
Respectfully submitted,
/s/ Don Bailey
